solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plumber, eg, is terrified to hold sink in

indicators.note: the phrase before it is said to hold something, so the letters are found running inside those words

explanation.surface: A tradesman so frightened that he daren't tackle a blocked kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' asks you to read straight through the end of 'Plumber', all of 'eg' and 'is', and the start of 'terrified'. 'Sink in' looks like part of the plumbing scene but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact sinks in it is taken on board, which is the mental sense of registering it.

clue.text: Weather is restricting holiday? On the contrary

indicators.note: one word restricting another encloses it
this reverses the stated relation, so the holiday word goes around the other rather than inside it

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: Bad weather confines people on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' alone would put the holiday word inside the other; 'On the contrary' flips that. 'Weather' is the verb, to withstand.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm is to withstand or hold out against it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Wagging tail, a dog's put on lead — in reality one's a fierce fighter

indicators.note: wagging means moving about, so these letters are jumbled
the lead letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A dog wagging its tail on a lead is really a ferocious brawler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wagging' rearranges TAILADOG into GLADIATO, and 'lead' gives R from 'reality'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena combatant who fought other men or beasts to the death was the archetypal fierce fighter.

clue.text: Founded Times Educational Supplement?

definitions.meaning: founded means established, as a firm is
the TES, short for the Times Educational Supplement, a UK teaching weekly, is the word set written upwards, as a down light is read

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the paper's initials TES are SET going up, which is how a down entry runs when reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have founded a company is to have established it, the phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: Chaps in television rejected part

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other
rejected means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: telly or tele is informal for television
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men on TV turned down a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reads TELE backwards as ELET; 'part' looks like a TV role but means a component.
explanation.definitionFit: A component or constituent of something larger is a part of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Cold in the morning for each person in tent

parts.note: C is the usual abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a.m. marks times in the morning
per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: A chilly early start for everyone sleeping under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staying in a tent on a campsite is a holidaymaker of exactly this kind, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: These letters from Scot could be so different

definitions.text: These letters from Scot could be so different

parts.words: These letters from Scot could be so different
parts.note: taking every other letter of the word Scot yields S and O, spelling so; the clue word different is the definition sense

explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes how 'so' comes from 'Scot': first and third letters. Separately it means 'different' or 'other', as in the American 'alternate route'.
explanation.definitionFit: In its adjectival sense this word means other or different, as in an alternative choice.

clue.text: Criticise one about to worry

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
I is the Roman numeral one
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Slating someone is likely to cause them anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To get into a fearful flap is a stronger form of worrying, a verb synonym.

clue.text: State of readiness for crisis, right after wine and beer

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right comes after the wine and beer

parts.note: red is red wine
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: An emergency is declared after a bout of wine and beer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the highest level of alert, a state of readiness when danger is imminent.

clue.text: See a tot playing with river mammal that likes to swim

indicators.note: the words are playing about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Watch a toddler splashing about with a playful aquatic animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the rearrangement of the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine creature of the Pacific coast spends nearly its whole life swimming and floating, so the description fits it.

clue.text: Son kept muscles firm on a trip

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
someone who keeps their muscles firm is toned

explanation.surface: A boy stays in shape while away on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a trip' reads as travel, but it is the drug sense of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on a drug trip is high, which is what the slang adjective describes.

clue.text: Mark's small belly

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pot or pot belly is a paunch

explanation.surface: Mark has a little paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name owning the belly; it is the definition, a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or dot on a surface is a mark, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Skirts with 50% off — politician's cut back

indicators.note: half the word is removed, leaving only its first three of six letters

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Clothing sold at half price because a politician slashed the budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stingy, spending less than is needed, is to economise meanly on something.

clue.text: Strange mice pair — conclusion from pupil derived from observation

indicators.note: the strange arrangement of these words means their letters are shuffled
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An odd pair of mice is what a schoolchild concluded from an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns MICEPAIR into EMPIRICA; 'conclusion from' takes the L ending 'pupil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained by experiment and experience rather than theory is the standard meaning of this scientific adjective.

clue.text: A trial limits time to give evidence

indicators.note: one word limits the other by enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a test is a trial, as in a trial run
T is the standard abbreviation for time in physics and timetables

explanation.surface: A court case allows a fixed period for witnesses to testify.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness or certify formally is a synonym for giving evidence.

clue.text: Euro's beginning to affect income, so cut expenditure

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter
to affect the words is to change them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The launch of the single currency hit earnings, so people spent less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes E from 'Euro's'; 'to affect' rearranges INCOMESO into CONOMISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend less money and live more frugally is to make savings, the same idea as cutting expenditure.

clue.text: Mark by yellow snake in the grass

parts.note: a distinguishing mark is a trait or characteristic
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Identify the yellow-striped serpent lurking in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake in the grass' suggests a reptile, but it is the idiom for a hidden betrayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake in the grass is an idiom for a treacherous person who betrays friends.

clue.text: Present a bit of money and hospital department provides medical care

parts.note: a treat is a present or indulgence

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its first letter

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A gift with a little cash and a hospital ward supply the healthcare.
explanation.definitionFit: Care given by doctors for an illness or injury is the standard medical sense of the word.

clue.text: Conserve energy after tedious person's party

indicators.note: the energy abbreviation comes after the dull person

parts.note: a conserve is jam
a bore is a tedious person
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Save your energy once the dullard arrives at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conserve' reads as the verb save; it is the noun, a fruit preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A large lively celebration, especially a Scout rally, is a big party.

clue.text: For a trip, flying, female leaves from here?

definitions.text: For a trip, flying, female leaves from here?

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered and rearranged
the letter leaves, so it is taken out of the words

explanation.surface: A woman flies off on her trip, and the question is where she departs from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops the F from FORATRIP, giving ORATRIP; 'flying' rearranges those letters. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the place itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers going by plane on a trip depart from this terminal facility, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Labour leader in tremendous demand

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ask is to demand

explanation.surface: The Labour Party leader is hugely sought after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party; it is the noun meaning a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work or chore to be done is a labour, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Smart Conservative backed party

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted Tory politician supported a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the revel word; 'party' looks political but means a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of intelligent or quick-witted is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Smack head?

parts.note: a smack is a small fishing boat, and the head of one is the person in command of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a blow; here it is a sailing fishing boat, and its head is the skipper.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipper in command of a vessel, here a fishing boat, is its master.

clue.text: Criminal act? He's free of sin!

indicators.note: a criminal twist on the words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man insists his offence was innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges ACTHES; the irony is that the answer means pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and virtuous, especially sexually, so untouched by sin.

clue.text: American can drink after this has been said?

definitions.text: American can drink after this has been said?

parts.note: in North American slang the can is the backside
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drinker in the USA may only start once the right words are spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a beer can, but it is US slang for the behind. The whole clue also describes the toast said before drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar toast spoken just before drinking, urging everyone to tip their glasses and drain them.

clue.text: Singer's note heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A vocalist hits a note that the audience hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests music; it is a banknote, a tenner being British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A high male voice part in a choir, and a man who sings it, so a type of singer.

clue.text: Toilet with child lock

parts.note: lat, short for latrine, is a toilet

explanation.surface: A lavatory fitted with a childproof fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A door fastening with a bar that drops into a catch is a simple kind of lock.

clue.text: Left part of church to decay

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: A neglected section of a church crumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall gradually into a worse state, as standards slip, is to decline or decay.

clue.text: High rank was in charge of police department

parts.note: someone who ran a team was in charge of it
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

explanation.surface: A senior officer once headed a police department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High rank' reads as seniority; here both words mean smelly, as of food gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is high or rank smells foul and has gone off, which is what spoiled butter or fat is called.

clue.text: Mends spa to regenerate humidity

indicators.note: to regenerate the words is to rebuild them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone restores a health resort to bring back its steamy atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Humidity is moisture in the air, a close synonym for a damp condition.

clue.text: Brought in sage — first leaves

indicators.note: the first letter departs from the word it begins

parts.note: a sage is wise or learned

explanation.surface: A herb is gathered in after its first leaves are picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb with leaves, but it means wise, as in learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Money brought in by work is money gained as wages, which is the past tense sense here.

clue.text: A Parisian somewhere in North Yorkshire is upset

parts.note: un is French for 'a', as a Parisian would say it
Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A French visitor to a Yorkshire town is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small market town in the Yorkshire Dales, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or throw someone off balance is a synonym for upsetting them.
